title: Oath and Ember
premise: Paloma Sterling, a mercenary bound by oath to a god who stopped answering a decade ago, discovers her own name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies kept by the dying last dragon. The prophecy names her the thief who must steal back a soul sold to the court beneath the mountain — the soul of Ember, the dragon's heir, whose fire keeps magic alive in the world beyond Paloma's magic-dead valley. Dragged out of the valley she never left, Paloma gathers an unlikely found family: a disgraced court scribe, a god-touched child, and the mercenary captain who once betrayed her. In the end, Paloma learns the silent god was never gone — it lives in every oath sworn in good faith — and she breaks her contract rather than complete it, giving her own soul's claim to free Ember, reigniting dragon-fire and unmaking the corrupt court, though it costs her the valley's protection forever.
about_author: Orsen Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing broken contracts and unpaid debts in municipal records, an experience that seeps into every bargain his characters strike. He writes fantasy about people who keep their word even when it ruins them, and he insists oaths are the oldest magic there is.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She takes a routine escort job through the magic-dead valley, establishing her mercenary life, her silent god, and the iron rule: no one leaves. When a stranger arrives carrying a book that shouldn't exist, her date of death — tonight — is written on its page. Beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Memory
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The stranger, scribe Wren Halloway, shows her the prophecy: a thief, a soul, a mountain, a guttering flame. The valley elders demand the book be burned; Paloma instead reads her own name aloud, and the words pull her through like a hook behind the ribs. Beat: the point of no return, chosen anyway.

chapters.title: A World With Teeth
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, disoriented. She wakes outside the valley for the first time in her life, where magic hums in everything and her god's silence feels louder. She is nearly killed by a ward-beast before being saved by Captain Ilsa Vane — the woman who betrayed her years ago. Beat: wonder curdling into old rage.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon's Bargain
chapters.summary: Paloma and reluctant ally Ilsa reach the dragon Ashfall, ancient and nearly fireless. He reveals the prophecy's terms: the soul beneath the mountain is Ember, his heir, sold to the Undercourt by Paloma's own order generations ago to buy the valley its safety. Beat: inheritance as debt, not gift.

chapters.title: What the Oath Costs
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Flashback woven into present: how her mercenary company swore itself to the silent god, and how Ilsa's betrayal left Paloma the only one still keeping the vow. She refuses to work with Ilsa; Wren mediates, revealing the prophecy requires all three. Beat: grudging truce over shared shame.

chapters.title: The City of Ledgers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The trio enters Vharn, a city where every citizen's soul is collateralized at birth. Wren navigates the archive-bureaucracy of the surface court, forging passage papers while teaching Paloma that power here is written, not fought. Beat: found family begins forming over forged documents.

chapters.title: The Child Who Hears Gods
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They shelter with Pip, an orphan who claims the silent god speaks through her — and repeats words Paloma swore alone in the dark years ago. Paloma wants to dismiss it; instead she weeps for the first time since her company died. Beat: grief given a voice.

chapters.title: Soldiers of the Silent Order
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Survivors of Paloma's old company, now serving the Undercourt, ambush the group. Ilsa confesses her betrayal was coerced — her own soul held as leverage. Paloma spares her, breaking her own rule. Beat: mercy as a crack in the armor.

chapters.title: Descent Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The group enters the Undercourt through a tithe-shaft, descending past strata of forfeited souls embedded in the rock like amber. The deeper they go, the more Paloma's oath burns — literally, marking her skin. Beat: awe and horror; the cost made visible.

chapters.title: Court of Unpaid Debts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Undercourt in full: magistrates who trade in obligation, beauty built entirely from what others owe. Wren recognizes the founding contracts — including one signed by Paloma's grandmother, selling Ember's soul. Beat: the personal becomes systemic; corruption has a paper trail.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Signature
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Confronting the contract, Paloma learns her valley's 'protection' was purchased with Ember — her whole life was funded by a stolen soul. Her identity cracks. Pip's presence keeps her from signing away her anger into the Court's hands. Beat: the lowest emotional point.

chapters.title: Ember in a Cage of Terms
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They find Ember: a young dragon reduced to a candle-flame inside a contractual cage, lucid and bitter after a century. Ember tests Paloma's motives cruelly — 'You come to feel better, not to free me.' Beat: the rescue target becomes a judge of character.

chapters.title: Loophole Hunters
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The team studies the soul-contract for flaws. Every loophole requires something unbearable: a life, a name, an oath freely broken. Ilsa offers her soul; Paloma refuses to let history repeat. Beat: sacrifice debated, deferred, dreaded.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Offer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The chief magistrate offers Paloma everything: Ember freed, her company resurrected, her god's voice restored — if she becomes the Court's enforcer, collecting debts across the world. Power dressed as rescue. She asks for one night to decide. Beat: temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: One Night of Almost
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating POVs. Around a smuggled fire, each character names what they'd take from the offer: Ilsa her honor, Wren her archive, Pip her family, Paloma her god's voice. Ember listens silently. By dawn they've all admitted the truth: none of it would be theirs. Beat: found family solidifies through shared refusal.

chapters.title: Refusal and Reprisal
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma rejects the magistrate, who reveals the trap: accepting or refusing, the Court keeps Ember unless the contract is broken from outside — by the silent god itself. But the god is silent because the Court owns its oldest debtor: Paloma's line. Beat: despair weaponized.

chapters.title: Ashfall's Last Fire
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ashfall, dying, spends his final flame breaching the Court's wards so the team can reach the contract-vault. His death-scene passes his remaining spark to Paloma — an inheritance she never wanted and cannot refuse. Beat: grief transmuted into duty.

chapters.title: The Vault of Names
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Inside the vault, Paloma finds her own true name recorded as collateral — the Court has owned her all along, which means her oath to the silent god was sworn with stolen goods. She realizes the god went silent out of shame, not abandonment. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Breaking the Oath
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Climax begins: Paloma deliberately breaks her sacred oath — the one act the Court cannot price, because it's freely given ruin. The breaking shatters her name-collateral and sends a shockwave through the Undercourt; the silent god answers at last, speaking through Pip and every honest oath ever sworn. Beat: catharsis through self-destruction.

chapters.title: The Court Comes Down
chapters.summary: Ensemble climax. Freed by the god's return, Ember ignites with inherited and returned fire; Wren voids the founding contracts; Ilsa holds the magistrates' guards at the doors. The Undercourt collapses as every soul it held reclaims itself. The magistrate, offered the same mercy he never gave, is simply released into a world that will remember. Beat: triumph without cruelty.

chapters.title: A Valley That Can Be Left
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Magic now flows everywhere, including the valley — its protective deadness gone, its purpose fulfilled. Paloma returns to bury her company's memory properly and finds she can walk out again freely. Ember, reborn in flame, offers her a place at a dragon's side. Beat: home redefined as people, not walls.

chapters.title: Oath and Ember
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue tone. A year later, Paloma leads a small found-family company — Ilsa, Wren, Pip, and Ember overhead — taking only contracts that free people from bad bargains. Her god speaks rarely now, but always when an oath is kept. Final line: she swears a new one, lightly, knowing it will hold. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
